original_question: Triangle-free non-planar graphs are already known to be forbidden subgraphs of bar k-visibility graphs. Determine whether there are other classes of forbidden subgraphs for bar k-visibility graphs.
target_in_paper: Open Problem 20 in Section 3.3 (Bar Visibility Graphs).
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s intended target very closely: it identifies the exact obstruction named in the paper—triangle-free non-planar graphs—and asks the same narrow follow-up question about whether there are additional forbidden subgraph classes for bar k-visibility graphs. It also stays at the right level of generality, rather than drifting into the broader characterization problem.
missing_details: The paper’s problem is specifically about bar k-visibility graphs as defined in Section 3.3: graphs represented by pairwise disjoint horizontal bars in the plane.
Adjacency must be defined exactly: two vertices are adjacent if and only if there exists a vertical segment between the corresponding bars that intersects at most k other bars.
The model is the strong bar k-visibility model discussed immediately before Open Problem 20.
The parameter k should be understood as a fixed nonnegative integer; the paper does not state a separate quantifier in Open Problem 20, but bar k-visibility graph is a k-parameterized class.
The paper asks about forbidden subgraphs, not induced subgraphs; that distinction should be made explicit to avoid broadening or changing the problem.

The question is existential and narrow: it asks whether there is any other class of forbidden subgraphs, not for a complete classification of all forbidden subgraphs and not for a full characterization of bar k-visibility graphs.
No algebraic ambient data (ring, field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, etc.) are relevant here; the hidden assumptions are entirely graph-theoretic.
refined_question: Fix a nonnegative integer k. A graph is a bar k-visibility graph if its vertices can be represented by pairwise disjoint horizontal bars in the plane so that two vertices are adjacent exactly when some vertical segment joining the corresponding bars intersects at most k other bars. It is known that no triangle-free non-planar graph can occur as a subgraph of a bar k-visibility graph. Is there any other class of graphs that is likewise forbidden as a subgraph of bar k-visibility graphs?
justification: This is the paper’s Open Problem 20 almost verbatim. The neighboring paragraph in Section 3.3 supplies the missing stand-alone context by defining bar k-visibility graphs and placing the question in the strong-visibility setting. The refined version stays narrower than Open Problem 19 ('Characterize bar k-visibility graphs') and preserves the exact intent of Open Problem 20: not a full characterization, but the specific search for additional forbidden subgraph classes beyond triangle-free non-planar graphs.
